result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.dfs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Perform depth-first search (DFS) traversal from a start node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23058-L23163){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.dfs( start, attr_name=None, return_list=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Depth-first search](/assets/graphs/dfs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same six-node graph searched depth-first from A. Numbered badges show the search running down one branch, A, B, D, F, E, before backing up to reach C last; the accent edges form a single long path. The result card lists the order A, B, D, F, E, C." width="100%"} DFS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking. Can return the visit order as a list, or store the position of each node in the traversal as a node attribute for visualization. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting node (integer ID or string label). [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store traversal position. If `None`, uses `dfs_order` as the attribute name. Position is 0-indexed (start node = `0`, first child = `1`, etc.). Nodes not visited get no attribute set. [return_list]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns list of node IDs in visit order. If `False`, stores positions as node attributes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[list[int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_list=` is `True`: list of node IDs visited in DFS order. If `return_list=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} DFS dives all the way down one branch of a tree before backtracking, which gives a very different visit order than BFS: ::: {#05801c18 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_balanced_tree(k=2, h=3) visited = graph.dfs(start=1) # Returns [1, 2, 4, 8, ...] (depth-first) visited ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Number of nodes : 15 Number of edges : 14 Directed : False Density : 0.13 Average degree (min, max) : 1.87 (1, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True Computations on nodes: - dfs(start=1) -> attr: 'dfs_order' (15 of 15 nodes) ``` ::: ::: As with `bfs()`, the traversal order can be stored as a node attribute instead of returned, which is useful for coloring nodes by visit order: ::: {#0ec86f6b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_balanced_tree(k=2, h=3) .dfs(start=1, return_list=False) .colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="dfs_order", palette="viridis" ) ) # Every node now has a "dfs_order" and a derived "color" attribute graph.get_node(1).attributes["dfs_order"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: On a simple path there's no branching, so DFS and BFS visit nodes in the same order: ::: {#8aa7a7fd .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) visited = graph.dfs(start=1) # Returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] visited ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Number of nodes : 5 Number of edges : 4 Directed : False Density : 0.40 Average degree (min, max) : 1.60 (1, 2) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True Computations on nodes: - dfs(start=1) -> attr: 'dfs_order' (5 of 5 nodes) ``` ::: :::
